title: 12-Week Climbing & Conditioning Program
subtitle: Bouldering performance  ·  Core & wind-sport conditioning  ·  Sciatica prevention
goals: Start: V5/V6 bouldering  |  Grade 20 lead  →  Target: V7+  |  Grade 22
schedule_line: Climb: Wed · Fri · Sun  |  Strength: Mon · Thu  |  Cardio: Tue  |  Recovery: Sat
overview: This 12-week program runs three goals simultaneously: improving bouldering and lead climbing grades; building core strength for the upcoming windy season; and protecting the lower back, coccyx, and finger/wrist joints. All home workouts are after-work (3:30pm+) sessions. Three phases of four weeks each build to a performance peak in Week 11, with a deliberate deload in Week 8.

weekly_schedule.focus: Upper antagonist, pull-up progression, tendon health

injuries.label: Lower back & sciatica
injuries.text: All core work uses anti-flexion and anti-rotation patterns only. Never do sit-ups, weighted crunches, or loaded spinal flexion. Sharp back pain or sciatic tingling → stop, switch to Mobility Variant B post-session, rest the next day. Symptoms beyond 48 hours → physiotherapy before continuing.

injuries.label: Coccyx
injuries.text: Cushion under knees in all seated stretches. Avoid direct tailbone pressure in floor exercises. If split squats or step-ups cause tailbone discomfort, reduce depth or substitute glute bridges.

injuries.label: Finger capsulitis
injuries.text: Favour open-hand and half-crimp throughout. Avoid full crimp while symptomatic. Finger & wrist care (Mobility, Post-workout Variant C) after upper-body and climbing sessions is non-negotiable — maintain it even on reduced-volume weeks. Acutely swollen or painful joint → skip loading, passive range-of-motion only.

injuries.label: Wrist pain
injuries.text: The finger-extensor strength work in your upper-body sessions and Mobility Variant C exist specifically for this. Do not skip them. If wrist pain increases after a session, ice for 10–15 min and note which grip preceded it.

injury_stop_rule: If sciatic symptoms (tingling, numbness, shooting pain down the leg) appear during any exercise, stop immediately. Never push through neurological symptoms.

phases.name: Foundation
intro: Every movement pattern introduced at low intensity with high form priority. Lower-body and core days introduce posterior chain and anti-rotation core work; upper-body days introduce upper antagonist work and — critically — the pull-up progression that runs through all 12 weeks. Mobility habits established from Day 1.
Home workout intensity: 6–7/10. Never grind. You should be able to add one more set.
Pull-up progression: scapular pulls (W1) → dead hangs (W2) → negatives 3×3 (W3) → negatives 3×5 (W4). The bar is there — use it from Day 1.
Cardio: Zone 2 only, building duration week by week.

phases.name: Development
intro: Load and complexity increase across all sessions. Lower-body days gain Nordic curl negatives, single-leg RDL, and reverse lunge. Upper-body days gain ring dips, archer rows, and escalating pull-up progression (negatives → first full pull-up attempts). The kilter board becomes a genuine training tool. Wind-sport conditioning circuit introduced from Week 6. Week 8 is a deliberate deload.
Home workout intensity: 7.5–8.5/10 in Weeks 5–7. Week 8 drops to 5/10.
Pull-up progression: negatives 3×5 (W5) → negatives 3×6 longer descent (W6) → first full pull-up attempts 3×2–4 (W7). Every rep counts.

phases.name: Performance
intro: Peak training across all domains. Core days gain standing band rotation and hollow body holds — the most important wind-sport and climbing core exercises in the program. Thursday pull-up progression moves to 3×5+ full reps or L-sit pull-up attempts. Climbing intensity peaks in Week 11. Week 12 is a light deload with deliberate grade tests on Friday and Sunday.
Home workout intensity: 8–9/10 in Weeks 9–11. Week 12 drops to 5/10.
Pull-up target: 3×5 full reps (W9) → 3×6 (W10) → 3×5+ with quality (W11). If still on negatives, aim for 10-second descents every rep.

weeks.tag: Learn every pattern · Establish mobility habit · Scapular pulls begin
notes: If any exercise produces pain (not effort — pain), reduce range of motion or revert to the easier variation. Form this week is the foundation everything else is built on.

items.text: Reverse lunge — 3×8 per side, rest 60s. Bodyweight, 3s lowering. Step BACK (lower spinal load than a forward lunge). Front knee stays over the front foot; drive up through the front heel. Torso tall.

climb.title: Climbing: New Set + Kilter Board Intro

items.text: Warm up 20 min.
New set: 50 min. Attempt every problem at grade. Don't pre-filter by style.
Kilter board intro (20–25°, 25 min): large juggy holds only. Goal is board familiarity, not difficulty. 4–5 easy problems, full rest between each.
Session total: ~100 min.
Drill: Lock-off drill — On three problems, pause at each lock-off (elbow bent) for 2 seconds before the next move. Strength through position.
items.name: Drill: Lock-off drill
items.detail: On three problems, pause at each lock-off (elbow bent) for 2 seconds before the next move. Strength through position.

alts.name: Drill: Silent feet
alts.detail: Place each foot so the shoe makes zero sound before the hands move. Forces precision and trust.

alts.name: Drill: Hover hands
alts.detail: Hover each hand 1 second above the hold before gripping. Cuts slapping and teaches reading the hold first.

alts.name: Drill: Flag challenge
alts.detail: Climb problems you've done using a flag (opposite leg out for balance) on every move you can.

items.text: 20-min warm-up on the wall.
Project: 2–3 burns on your limit problem, 4–5 min full rests. Stop if quality degrades.
Kilter board (25 min): same introductory approach as your previous climbing session — easy angle, large holds, body position focus.
Drill: Down-climb 3 — Down-climb three problems instead of jumping off. Eccentric control and body awareness.
items.name: Drill: Down-climb 3
items.detail: Down-climb three problems instead of jumping off. Eccentric control and body awareness.

alts.name: Drill: Straight arms
alts.detail: Climb with the arms as straight as possible, hips close to the wall. Relax the grip by ~20%.

alts.name: Drill: Slow motion
alts.detail: Take 5 seconds per move. Stand still on each hold for a breath before moving.

alts.name: Drill: Deadpoint control
alts.detail: Pick moves just out of reach. Control the deadpoint and catch the hold without swinging.

climb.title: Climbing: Lead, Attempt Grade 19

items.text: Lead warm-up at 15–16 for 15–20 min.
4–5 laps at grade 17–18 with full rests.
Attempt grade 19 at least twice with genuine rest (7 min) between. Work out the sequence if it doesn't go.
Drill: Find the rest — On each route find at least three positions where you can drop an arm and shake out. Use them every time.
items.name: Drill: Find the rest
items.detail: On each route find at least three positions where you can drop an arm and shake out. Use them every time.

alts.name: Drill: Clip from the best stance
alts.detail: Reach no higher than needed to clip and clip from the most stable stance. Shake out before the clip.

alts.name: Drill: Switch-hand clipping
alts.detail: Clip with the weaker hand on the next route. Builds efficiency on routes where the clip hand isn't obvious.

alts.detail: Hover each hand above the hold before grabbing. Keeps the rope drag down and the pace controlled.

intro: DELOAD WEEK. Every session deliberately reduced in volume and intensity. Adaptations from Weeks 5–7 consolidate NOW — skipping or shortening the deload is a mistake.

items.text: Warm up 20 min.
New set: genuine attempts at V6–V7. Project 1 problem — spend time on it rather than ticking and moving on.

alts.detail: Place each foot so the shoe makes zero sound before the hands move. Forces precision and trust.

climb.title: Climbing: Fresh Limit Boulders + Kilter Power

items.text: Warm up thoroughly — 20 min.
items.name: Warm up thoroughly
items.detail: 20 min.

items.text: Limit bouldering: 4–5 genuine attempts on hardest problems in the gym. 5-min full rests. Best climbing of the week.
Kilter board (45°, 35 min): power circuits — 3 problems ×3 sets, full rests.
items.name: Kilter board (45°, 35 min): power circuits
items.detail: 3 problems ×3 sets, full rests.

items.text: Drill: Flag challenge — Climb problems you've done using a flag (opposite leg out for balance) on every move you can.
items.name: Drill: Flag challenge
items.detail: Climb problems you've done using a flag (opposite leg out for balance) on every move you can.

alts.name: Drill: Open-hand only
alts.detail: On V3–V4 problems use only open-hand grips — no crimping. Easier on a sore capsule and builds finger-friendly habits.

alts.name: Drill: Down-climb 3
alts.detail: Down-climb three problems instead of jumping off. Eccentric control and body awareness.

alts.name: Drill: Straight arms
alts.detail: Climb with the arms as straight as possible, hips close to the wall. Relax the grip by ~20%.

items.text: Lead warm-up at 17–18 for 20 min.
4–5 laps at grade 19–20 with full rests.
1–2 redpoint attempts at grade 21. If you haven't sent it yet, this is the window.
Pump management: when the forearms load, stay on the wall, breathe deliberately, climb through it. This is how lead endurance is trained.
Drill: Switch-hand clipping — Clip with the weaker hand on the next route. Builds efficiency on routes where the clip hand isn't obvious.

alts.detail: Hover each hand above the hold before grabbing. Keeps the rope drag down and the pace controlled.

alts.name: Drill: 4×4 endurance
alts.detail: Four routes back-to-back at 2 grades below your limit, 2-min rest, repeat 3 rounds. Pump management.

alts.name: Drill: Controlled lead falls
alts.detail: Practise short controlled falls on clean overhanging gym routes with a trusted belayer. Confidence for the grade tests.

items.text: 5-min warm-up.

items.text: Immediately after: 3 rounds of standing band rotation ×15/side, lateral lunge ×10/side. Rest 60s between rounds.

Drill: Silent feet — Place each foot so the shoe makes zero sound before the hands move. Forces precision and trust.
items.name: Drill: Silent feet
items.detail: Place each foot so the shoe makes zero sound before the hands move. Forces precision and trust.

alts.name: Drill: Hover hands
alts.detail: Hover each hand 1 second above the hold before gripping. Cuts slapping and teaches reading the hold first.

alts.name: Drill: Flag challenge
alts.detail: Climb problems you've done using a flag (opposite leg out for balance) on every move you can.

alts.name: Drill: Open-hand only
alts.detail: On V3–V4 problems use only open-hand grips — no crimping. Easier on a sore capsule and builds finger-friendly habits.

alts.detail: Climb a lap focusing only on rope handling: clip, check the rope path, lower off smoothly.

weeks.name: Performance — Peak Week
intro: PEAK WEEK. Climbing sessions are the primary stimulus. Do not add extra sessions. Performance comes from quality, not volume. Sleep this week matters more than any extra set.
notes: Sleep (7–9 hours) has a measurable positive effect on climbing performance, reaction time, and injury resistance. Prioritise it this week above any extra training.

alts.name: Drill: Straight arms
alts.detail: Climb with the arms as straight as possible, hips close to the wall. Relax the grip by ~20%.

alts.name: Drill: Slow motion
alts.detail: Take 5 seconds per move. Stand still on each hold for a breath before moving.

items.text: Warm up very thoroughly — 25 min.

items.detail: 25 min.

items.text: Project: 4–5 burns, 5–6 min full rests. Approach each burn calm and methodical. This is the day to send your project.
Kilter board: 2 limit problems ×2 burns each if energy clearly allows.

alts.name: Drill: Lock-off drill
alts.detail: On three problems, pause at each lock-off (elbow bent) for 2 seconds before the next move. Strength through position.

alts.name: Drill: Silent feet
alts.detail: Place each foot so the shoe makes zero sound before the hands move. Forces precision and trust.

alts.name: Drill: Hover hands
alts.detail: Hover each hand 1 second above the hold before gripping. Cuts slapping and teaches reading the hold first.

items.text: Lead warm-up at 17–18 for 20–25 min. Take longer than usual.
3 laps at grade 19–20.
Grade test: best attempts at grade 21 and/or 22 with 10-min minimum rests between.
Document the outcome — what felt possible, where it broke down, what has definitively changed since Week 1.
items.name: Document the outcome
items.detail: what felt possible, where it broke down, what has definitively changed since Week 1.

items.text: Drill: Find the rest — On each route find at least three positions where you can drop an arm and shake out. Use them every time.
items.name: Drill: Find the rest
items.detail: On each route find at least three positions where you can drop an arm and shake out. Use them every time.

alts.name: Drill: Clip from the best stance
alts.detail: Reach no higher than needed to clip and clip from the most stable stance. Shake out before the clip.

alts.name: Drill: Switch-hand clipping
alts.detail: Clip with the weaker hand on the next route. Builds efficiency on routes where the clip hand isn't obvious.

alts.name: Drill: Quiet hands
alts.detail: Hover each hand above the hold before grabbing. Keeps the rope drag down and the pace controlled.

weeks.name: Deload + Reflect
weeks.tag: Recover · Boulder grade test Friday · Review the program
intro: FINAL WEEK. Reduced volume everywhere. One climbing session is your boulder grade test and another is a relaxed lead session. Use this week to review what changed and plan the next cycle.
notes: Compare Week 12 to Week 1. Boulder grade? Lead grade? How's the lower back? Fingers and wrists? What sessions did you consistently skip and why? These answers define what the next 12-week block should prioritise.

upper.note: Deload: half the sets, no grinding. The strength is consolidating — keep the movement crisp and leave energy in the tank.

items.text: Dead bug — 2×10 per side, rest 30s. Lower back pressed completely flat into the mat. If the back arches as the leg lowers, you've gone too far — reduce range. Slow, controlled breathing.
items.name: Dead bug
items.detail: 2×10 per side, rest 30s. Lower back pressed completely flat into the mat. If the back arches as the leg lowers, you've gone too far — reduce range. Slow, controlled breathing.

alts.name: Heel-tap dead bug
alts.detail: Only tap the heel to the floor; keep the knees bent at 90°.

alts.name: Banded dead bug
alts.detail: Hold a band overhead in both hands and keep it taut as the limbs extend.

alts.name: Dead bug with backpack press
alts.detail: Press a light backpack toward the ceiling throughout the rep.

alts.name: Leg-lower dead bug
alts.detail: Arms stay up; lower one straight leg at a time to just above the floor.

alts.name: Arms-only bird-dog
alts.detail: Keep both knees down; just reach alternate arms.

alts.name: Bird-dog with band row
alts.detail: Hold a band under the hand; after extending, pull the elbow back toward the hip.

alts.name: Bear hold (knees 2cm up)
alts.detail: Hover the knees just off the floor for 20–30s with a flat back.

alts.name: Plank shoulder taps
alts.detail: Feet wide, tap alternate shoulders without letting the hips rotate.

items.name: Side plank

alts.name: Side plank from the knees
alts.detail: Bottom knee down; keep the line from head to knee straight.

alts.name: Side plank with top-leg lift
alts.detail: Raise the top leg 10 times while holding the plank.

alts.name: Copenhagen plank (short lever)
alts.detail: Top knee on a chair, bottom leg hangs. Shorter lever than the full version.

alts.name: Side plank with band row
alts.detail: Hold a band under the bottom hand and row the top elbow to the ribs.

items.cue: Stack hips and feet. Squeeze the bottom glute to stop the hips dropping. The lateral core used to trim a board in swell.

Mobility Variant A followed by Variant B back-to-back (40 min). Best preparation for next cycle.
Easy climbing — V3–V4. No pressure. Smooth movement, enjoy the wall.

Drill: Silent feet — Place each foot so the shoe makes zero sound before the hands move. Forces precision and trust.
items.name: Drill: Silent feet

alts.name: Drill: Hover hands

alts.name: Drill: Flag challenge

alts.name: Drill: Open-hand only
alts.detail: On V3–V4 problems use only open-hand grips — no crimping. Easier on a sore capsule and builds finger-friendly habits.

alts.name: Drill: Down-climb 3

Drill: Exhale on every clip — Deliberately exhale on every clip and before every hard sequence. Reduces pump and tension.

items.detail: Deliberately exhale on every clip and before every hard sequence. Reduces pump and tension.

alts.name: Drill: Find the rest
alts.detail: On each route find at least three positions where you can drop an arm and shake out. Use them every time.

alts.name: Drill: Clip from the best stance
alts.detail: Reach no higher than needed to clip and clip from the most stable stance. Shake out before the clip.

alts.name: Drill: Switch-hand clipping
alts.detail: Clip with the weaker hand on the next route. Builds efficiency on routes where the clip hand isn't obvious.

nutrition: Moderate deficit of 300–500kcal/day combined with 1.6–2g protein per kg of bodyweight (160–200g/day at current weight). A loss rate of 0.5–1%/week preserves strength. Over 12 weeks expect 5–6kg loss — meaningful progress without compromising performance.
Protein priority: hit targets every day, especially on climbing days and the day after hard sessions.
Hydration: 2–3L daily baseline; more on hot or high-output days.
Pre-workout meal: eat carbohydrate + protein 1–2 hours before home sessions. Training on empty after a full working day produces poor performance.
Do not cut aggressively in Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12). Maintain the deficit but prioritise fuelling climbing sessions.

strength_guide.title: How hard to train (reps in reserve)
strength_guide.text: RIR = reps in reserve. At 2 RIR you stop a set with two clean reps still possible. Main lifts sit at 2 RIR in Phases 2–3 (1–3 RIR in Phase 1). Never grind: if form breaks down, the set is over.

strength_guide.title: Loading with a backpack
strength_guide.text: Pack books or water bottles and weigh the bag. Hold it at your chest for squats and hinges (goblet style), in one hand for carries, on the hips for thrusts, and clamp it between the ankles for weighted dips. Add ~2kg only when every set finishes at 2+ RIR.

strength_guide.title: Progression rule
strength_guide.text: Double progression: stay at the same load until you hit the top of the rep range on every set, then add load and drop back to the bottom of the range. If you stall for two weeks, swap in a variation from the Swap menu.

strength_guide.title: Tempo & rest
strength_guide.text: Lower under control (3 seconds on the way down) and rest fully on heavy sets — the rest chips count it down automatically after you tick an exercise. Longer rests make heavy sets stronger.

strength_guide.title: Spine, tailbone and fingers
strength_guide.text: No loaded spinal flexion, ever. Keep hinges flat-backed. Stop on any sciatic tingling, numbness or shooting pain. Cushion the tailbone for floor work. Finger and wrist care (Mobility, Variant C) stays in even when you cut volume.

strength_guide.title: Variations
strength_guide.text: Every exercise has a Swap menu: easier (when pain, tiredness or form calls for it), harder (when 2 RIR is easy) and sideways (to change the stimulus). A swap stays for that session only, so you can try new things freely.

revlunge.name: Reverse lunge
revlunge.cue: Step BACK (lower spinal load than a forward lunge). Front knee stays over the front foot; drive up through the front heel. Torso tall.

alts.name: Static split squat
alts.detail: Same stance, no stepping. Lower straight down and up, keeping the front shin near-vertical.

alts.name: Deficit reverse lunge
alts.detail: Stand with the front foot on a 5–10cm step so the knee travels further. Slow 3s lowering.

alts.name: Backpack reverse lunge
alts.detail: Hold a loaded backpack at your chest. Keep the ribs down, no leaning back.

alts.name: Curtsy lunge
alts.detail: Step back and across behind the front leg. Works the glute medius — the hip stabiliser.

alts.name: Walking lunge (short stride)
alts.detail: Short strides, tall torso. Keep the front knee tracking over the middle toe.

alts.name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
alts.detail: Dumbbells at your sides. Step back, lower, and drive up through the front heel. Keep the torso tall.

stepup.name: Step-ups
stepup.cue: Drive through the heel of the working leg; control the step down slowly. The working leg does all the work — do not push off with the trailing leg. Use a box or chair with the knee at or above hip height.

alts.name: Low step-up
alts.detail: Use a lower step and keep the same slow lowering.

alts.name: Backpack high step-up
alts.detail: Hold a loaded backpack at your chest and use a box that puts the knee above hip height.

alts.name: Slow step-down (5s)
alts.detail: Step up normally, then take 5 seconds to lower. Great for knee resilience.

alts.name: Lateral step-up
alts.detail: Stand side-on to the box. Same drive, more glute medius.

alts.name: Step-up with knee drive
alts.detail: Drive the free knee up at the top and balance for 1s before lowering.

bss.name: Bulgarian split squats
bss.cue: Rear foot elevated on a chair, front foot far enough forward that the shin stays near-vertical. Upright torso, lower straight down. Stop if the tailbone or knee complains and reduce depth.

alts.name: Split squat (rear foot on floor)
alts.detail: Same stance with the back foot on the floor. Hold a wall for balance.

alts.name: Backpack-loaded split squat
alts.detail: Hold a loaded backpack at your chest (goblet position). Add load only if you keep 2 reps in reserve.

alts.name: Split squat with 3s pause
alts.detail: Pause 3 seconds in the bottom position. The pause is where the strength is built.

alts.name: Rear-foot-elevated reverse lunge
alts.detail: Step back into the lunge instead of holding the position — more dynamic, a different stimulus.

alts.name: Rear foot in rings
alts.detail: Rear foot in hanging rings. Stability demand goes way up — drop the load.

alts.name: Dumbbell split squat
alts.detail: Rear foot on a chair, a dumbbell in each hand, torso upright. Lower straight down and drive up through the front heel.

calf.name: Single-leg calf raise
calf.cue: Toes on the edge of a step. Rise tall onto the ball of the foot, pause 1s at the top, lower for 3s to a full stretch. Calf and foot strength is what keeps you stable on small footholds.

alts.name: Two-leg calf raise
alts.detail: Both feet on the step, same slow lowering.

alts.name: Backpack-loaded calf raise
alts.detail: Hold a loaded backpack in one hand and the wall with the other.

alts.name: Toe-in / toe-out calf raise
alts.detail: Rotate the feet in or out between sets to hit the calf from different angles.

alts.name: Tibialis raise
alts.detail: Heels on the floor, back against a wall, lift toes up. Shin strength balances the calf and protects the shins.

glutebridge.name: Single-leg glute bridge
glutebridge.cue: Drive through the heel, squeeze the glute at the top. Non-working knee stays at 90°. Ribs down — don't arch the lower back.

alts.name: Two-leg glute bridge
alts.detail: Both feet down, 3s squeeze at the top.

alts.name: Feet-elevated single-leg bridge
alts.detail: Working foot on a low chair. Longer range, harder glutes.

alts.name: Backpack-loaded bridge
alts.detail: Backpack resting on the hips (pad it with a towel).

alts.name: Bridge march
alts.detail: From a double bridge, alternate lifting each foot while the hips stay level.

alts.name: Banded bridge
alts.detail: Light band above the knees; push the knees out through the rep.

alts.name: Dumbbell hip thrust
alts.detail: Upper back on a chair or sofa, dumbbell across the hips (padded). Drive the hips to a flat line, squeeze for 1 second, lower slowly.

hipthrust.name: Single-leg hip thrust
hipthrust.cue: Upper back on a sofa or sturdy chair, one foot planted, other knee hugged. Drive the hips up to a flat line from shoulder to knee, ribs down — no arching the lower back. Squeeze for 1s at the top.

alts.name: Double-leg hip thrust
alts.detail: Both feet planted. Add load before going to one leg.

alts.name: Backpack hip thrust
alts.detail: Backpack on the hips (padded). Pause 2s at the top.

alts.name: Frog pump
alts.detail: Soles of the feet together, knees out. Short range, big glute squeeze — high reps.

alts.name: Banded hip thrust
alts.detail: Light band above the knees; keep the knees pressed out.

alts.name: Dumbbell hip thrust
alts.detail: Upper back on a chair or sofa, dumbbell across the hips (padded). Drive the hips to a flat line, squeeze for 1 second, lower slowly.

nordic.name: Nordic curl negatives
nordic.cue: Feet firmly anchored (heavy sofa, door-hinge band). From kneeling, lower toward the floor as slowly as possible — target 8–10 seconds. Catch with your hands. Do not collapse. One of the most effective posterior-chain exercises available without equipment.

alts.name: Band-assisted Nordic
alts.detail: Loop a band around your chest anchored overhead to reduce the load, or use a bigger catch with the hands.

alts.name: Slider hamstring curl
alts.detail: Lie on your back, heels on a towel on a smooth floor. Bridge up, drag the heels out and back in slowly.

alts.name: Nordic with 5s hold
alts.detail: Pause 5 seconds at the lowest point you can control before catching yourself.

alts.name: Single-leg slider curl
alts.detail: As the slider curl, but one leg at a time. Hips stay high.

slrdl.name: Single-leg RDL
slrdl.cue: Hinge at the hip with a soft bend in the standing knee. Raised leg trails and keeps the hips square. Back flat — the most important cue. Light fingertip on a wall for balance. Stop at once if sciatic symptoms appear.

alts.name: Kickstand RDL
alts.detail: Back foot lightly on the floor for balance; most of the load stays on the front leg.

alts.name: Backpack-loaded single-leg RDL
alts.detail: Hug a loaded backpack to your chest, or hold it in the hand opposite the standing leg.

alts.name: Single-leg RDL with 3s lowering
alts.detail: Same movement, 3 seconds on the way down.

alts.name: Single-leg RDL to knee drive
alts.detail: Stand up and drive the free knee to hip height, balance 1s, repeat.

alts.name: Offset-load RDL
alts.detail: Load in the hand on the same side as the standing leg — a different balance challenge.

alts.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
alts.detail: Soft knees, dumbbells close to the legs, push the hips back with a flat back to mid-shin, then drive the hips forward. Stop at once if sciatic symptoms appear.

goodmorning.name: Band good mornings
goodmorning.cue: Anchor the band under both feet, hinge from the hips with a flat back. Cue: 'push hips back, not chest forward.'

alts.name: Hip hinge with a broom handle
alts.detail: Hold a stick along the spine (head, upper back, tailbone touching) and hinge. Trains the flat-back pattern.

alts.name: Backpack RDL (hugged to chest)
alts.detail: Hug a loaded backpack and hinge to mid-shin. Keep the back flat and stop if you feel any sciatic symptoms.

alts.name: Band good morning with 3s pause
alts.detail: Pause 3 seconds at the bottom of every rep.

alts.name: Band pull-through
alts.detail: Anchor the band behind you, hold it between the legs and hinge. Great glute lockout.

alts.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
alts.detail: Soft knees, dumbbells close to the legs, push the hips back with a flat back to mid-shin, then drive the hips forward. Stop at once if sciatic symptoms appear.

pistol.name: Box pistol squat
pistol.cue: Stand in front of a chair on one leg, free leg extended forward, arms forward for balance. Sit down slowly (4s), touch the seat lightly, and stand up without bouncing. Use a higher seat if the knee complains.

alts.name: Assisted pistol (hold a ring)
alts.detail: Hold hanging rings or a door frame for assistance and reduce the pull as you get stronger.

alts.name: Slow single-leg sit-down
alts.detail: Lower for 5s on one leg and stand with both legs. Eccentric strength comes first.

alts.name: Counterbalanced pistol
alts.detail: Hold a backpack out in front for counterbalance.

alts.name: Skater squat
alts.detail: Back knee lowers toward the floor behind you. Less depth demand, more balance work.

deadbug.name: Dead bug
deadbug.cue: Lower back pressed completely flat into the mat. If the back arches as the leg lowers, you've gone too far — reduce range. Slow, controlled breathing.

alts.name: Heel-tap dead bug
alts.detail: Only tap the heel to the floor; keep the knees bent at 90°.

alts.name: Banded dead bug
alts.detail: Hold a band overhead in both hands and keep it taut as the limbs extend.

alts.name: Dead bug with backpack press
alts.detail: Press a light backpack toward the ceiling throughout the rep.

alts.name: Leg-lower dead bug
alts.detail: Arms stay up; lower one straight leg at a time to just above the floor.

birddog.name: Bird-dog
birddog.cue: Extend the opposite arm and leg simultaneously and pause at the top. Hips stay level throughout — don't rotate.

alts.name: Arms-only bird-dog
alts.detail: Keep both knees down; just reach alternate arms.

alts.name: Bird-dog with band row
alts.detail: Hold a band under the hand; after extending, pull the elbow back toward the hip.

alts.name: Bear hold (knees 2cm up)
alts.detail: Hover the knees just off the floor for 20–30s with a flat back.

alts.name: Plank shoulder taps
alts.detail: Feet wide, tap alternate shoulders without letting the hips rotate.

pallof.name: Band Pallof press
pallof.cue: Anchor at chest height. Press both hands away and hold. This is anti-rotation — resist the pull, don't let the torso turn.

alts.name: Half-kneeling Pallof press
alts.detail: Kneel on a cushion; easier balance, same anti-rotation.

alts.name: Pallof press with step-out
alts.detail: Press out, then take two lateral steps away from the anchor and back.

alts.name: Pallof press to overhead
alts.detail: After pressing out, raise both arms overhead and bring them back.

alts.name: Tall-kneeling Pallof with lift
alts.detail: Tall-kneeling, press out and lift the hands to forehead height.

alts.name: Plank shoulder taps
alts.detail: High plank with feet wide. Tap alternate shoulders without letting the hips rotate. Slow and square.

pallofreach.name: Pallof press to reach
pallofreach.cue: After pressing out, extend one arm overhead while maintaining anti-rotation tension, return, switch. Trains the overhead stability used in dynamic climbing.

alts.name: Standard Pallof press
alts.detail: Skip the overhead reach and focus on resisting rotation.

alts.name: Pallof press to reach in half-kneeling
alts.detail: Half-kneeling makes the hips less stable.

alts.name: Plank shoulder taps
alts.detail: High plank with feet wide. Tap alternate shoulders without letting the hips rotate. Slow and square.

sideplank.name: Side plank
sideplank.cue: Stack hips and feet. Squeeze the bottom glute to stop the hips dropping. The lateral core used to trim a board in swell.

alts.name: Side plank from the knees
alts.detail: Bottom knee down; keep the line from head to knee straight.

alts.name: Side plank with top-leg lift
alts.detail: Raise the top leg 10 times while holding the plank.

alts.name: Copenhagen plank (short lever)
alts.detail: Top knee on a chair, bottom leg hangs. Shorter lever than the full version.

alts.name: Side plank with band row
alts.detail: Hold a band under the bottom hand and row the top elbow to the ribs.

sideplankreach.name: Side plank with reach-through
sideplankreach.cue: From side plank, reach the top arm under the body then back overhead — controlled rotation, hips don't drop.

alts.name: Side plank from the knees
alts.detail: Same reach, bottom knee on the mat.

alts.name: Side plank reach with top-leg lift
alts.detail: Raise the top leg as the arm reaches back overhead.

sideplankrot.name: Side plank rotation
sideplankrot.cue: From side plank, rotate the top arm under the body (thread-the-needle) and return. Controlled rotation, hips don't drop.

alts.name: Side plank from the knees
alts.detail: Same rotation from the knees.

alts.name: Side plank rotation with band resist
alts.detail: Hold a light band for resistance as you open the chest.

copenhagen.name: Copenhagen plank
copenhagen.cue: Side plank with the top foot (or knee) on a chair, the bottom leg hanging free. Lift the hips until the body is straight and hold. Adductor and lateral-core strength; start with the knee on the chair and move the foot out as you get stronger.

alts.name: Copenhagen from the knee
alts.detail: Top knee on a chair — the shortest lever.

alts.name: Copenhagen with leg lift
alts.detail: Foot on the chair; lift the bottom leg to meet it and lower.

alts.name: Side-lying adductor lift
alts.detail: Bottom leg lifts toward the ceiling with the top leg supported on a cushion.

hollow.name: Hollow body hold
hollow.cue: Arms overhead, legs raised slightly (20–30°), lower back pressed completely flat into the mat — zero gap between the back and the mat. This is the core tension position used on every overhanging boulder problem. If the back lifts, bring the legs higher until it stays flat.

alts.name: Tucked hollow hold
alts.detail: Knees bent toward the chest, arms by your sides.

alts.name: Hollow hold with band pull-over
alts.detail: Hold a light band overhead and keep it taut while the ribs stay down.

alts.name: Hollow hold with small flutter kicks
alts.detail: Keep the back flat and kick tiny — no big swings.

alts.name: Reverse-plank hold
alts.detail: Face up, hands behind you, hips lifted. Opens the front of the body while keeping the core on.

ringfallout.name: Ring fallout
ringfallout.cue: Kneel with the hands in rings hung low. Brace the abs, ribs down, and roll the rings forward only as far as the lower back stays neutral — any sag means stop earlier. Pull back by squeezing the lats and abs. Anti-extension strength.

alts.name: Wall roll-out
alts.detail: Forearms on a wall, roll the body away and back.

alts.name: Ring body saw (long lever)
alts.detail: From a plank on the rings, move the whole body forward and back a few centimetres.

alts.name: Towel body saw
alts.detail: Feet on a towel on a smooth floor, forearms down; push back and forth.

alts.name: Plank walk-out
alts.detail: From standing, walk the hands out to a long plank and back; do not let the hips sag.

standrot.name: Standing band rotation
standrot.cue: Anchor at hip height. Hips stay square — only the torso rotates. Trains the same oblique pattern as harness management and board trim in wind sports.

alts.name: Half-kneeling band rotation
alts.detail: Kneel on a cushion for stability.

alts.name: Band woodchop (high to low)
alts.detail: Anchor above head height and chop diagonally to the opposite hip.

alts.name: Landmine-style band press-and-rotate
alts.detail: Anchor low and press out, rotating through the hips and trunk.

alts.name: Plank shoulder taps
alts.detail: High plank with feet wide. Tap alternate shoulders without letting the hips rotate. Slow and square.

carry.name: Suitcase carry
carry.cue: Hold a loaded backpack in one hand and walk tall — don't lean away from the weight, ribs stacked over the hips. Builds the lateral core that stabilises you on steep walls and in harness/board work.

alts.name: Lighter suitcase carry
alts.detail: Reduce the load by a third and walk slower.

alts.name: Farmer's carry (two bags)
alts.detail: Carry a loaded bag in each hand.

alts.name: Waiter carry
alts.detail: Backpack held overhead in one hand, ribs down.

alts.name: Front-loaded backpack carry
alts.detail: Hug the backpack to your chest and walk.

alts.name: Dumbbell suitcase carry
alts.detail: One dumbbell in one hand, walk tall without leaning away from the weight. Ribs stacked over hips.

pushup.name: Push-ups
pushup.cue: Full range, chest to the mat. Elbows at about 45° from the body. Keep the body in one straight line.

alts.name: Incline push-ups
alts.detail: Hands on a chair or counter; same full range.

alts.name: Decline push-ups
alts.detail: Feet on a chair, same tempo.

alts.name: Archer push-ups
alts.detail: Wide hands; lower to one side while the other arm stays straight.

alts.name: Push-ups on fists
alts.detail: Fists on the mat for a neutral wrist — kind to sore wrists.

alts.name: Tempo push-ups (4s down, 1s pause)
alts.detail: Slower tempo, same range.

alts.name: Dumbbell floor press
alts.detail: Lie on the floor, elbows at about 45°, press the dumbbells up and lower until the upper arms touch the floor.

ringpush.name: Ring push-ups
ringpush.cue: Control the rings. Turn them out slightly at the top. Knees on the floor is fine. Tempo: 3 seconds down.

alts.name: Ring push-ups from the knees
alts.detail: Knees down; same tempo.

alts.name: Feet-elevated ring push-ups
alts.detail: Feet on a chair. Shoulder and chest load go up.

alts.name: Ring push-up with RTO hold
alts.detail: At the top, turn the rings out and hold 2 seconds.

alts.name: Ring push-up with 3s bottom pause
alts.detail: Pause at the bottom for 3 seconds before pressing.

alts.name: Dumbbell floor press
alts.detail: Lie on the floor, elbows at about 45°, press the dumbbells up and lower until the upper arms touch the floor.

pike.name: Pike push-ups
pike.cue: Hips high (inverted V), lower the crown of the head toward the floor between the hands.

alts.name: Incline pike push-up
alts.detail: Hands on a low chair.

alts.name: Feet-elevated pike push-up
alts.detail: Feet on a chair so the torso is more vertical.

alts.name: Wall handstand hold
alts.detail: Chest to the wall, hold 20–30s. Overhead shoulder strength without the pressing.

alts.name: Wall HSPU negative
alts.detail: Kick up to the wall, lower slowly, step down. Add only when pike push-ups feel easy.

alts.name: Dumbbell overhead press
alts.detail: Stand tall, ribs down, press the dumbbells overhead without arching the lower back. Lower with control.

ringdips.name: Ring dips
ringdips.cue: Lower to about 90° elbow angle — not past 90° early on. 3-second descent. If the rings wobble excessively, use dip bars and move to rings later.

alts.name: Dip-bar dips
alts.detail: Same range on parallel bars, which are more stable.

alts.name: Ring dips with 3s pause
alts.detail: Pause 3 seconds at the bottom.

alts.name: Weighted dips
alts.detail: Backpack clamped between the ankles or held in the lap. Only if you can do 3×10 bodyweight.

alts.name: Slow negative dips (5s)
alts.detail: Lower for 5 seconds and step up, if the press is not available.

alts.name: Close-grip push-ups
alts.detail: Hands under the chest, elbows brushing the ribs. Triceps-focused. Use fists if the wrists are sore.

alts.name: Chair dips
alts.detail: Hands on the edge of a sturdy chair, legs bent, lower to about 90° and press back up. Stop if the shoulders pinch.

bardips.name: Straight-bar dips
bardips.cue: More stable than rings, allows harder loading. Chest forward, shoulders away from the ears.

alts.name: Dip-bar dips
alts.detail: Use parallel bars if the straight bar is too awkward.

alts.name: Weighted straight-bar dips
alts.detail: Add a light backpack when you can do 3×10.

alts.name: Ring dips
alts.detail: Less stability, more shoulder control.

alts.name: Close-grip push-ups
alts.detail: Hands under the chest, elbows brushing the ribs. Triceps-focused. Use fists if the wrists are sore.

alts.name: Chair dips
alts.detail: Hands on the edge of a sturdy chair, legs bent, lower to about 90° and press back up. Stop if the shoulders pinch.

dipsupport.name: Dip support hold
dipsupport.cue: Lock out at the top. Shoulders down and back — do not shrug.

alts.name: Dip support with tuck
alts.detail: Tuck the knees while holding the lockout.

alts.name: Ring support hold
alts.detail: Do the same hold on the rings, turning them out slightly.

tucksit.name: Tuck-sit on dip bars
tucksit.cue: Lock out at the top with the knees tucked up. Don't round the lower back; push the bars down.

alts.name: Dip support hold
alts.detail: Hold lockout with straight legs hanging.

alts.name: One-leg-extended L-sit
alts.detail: Extend one leg forward while the other stays tucked.

alts.name: L-sit hold
alts.detail: Both legs extended forward.

alts.name: Floor tuck-sit
alts.detail: Hands flat on the floor beside the hips, press down to lift the hips and tuck the knees. Shoulders pushed down, back rounded slightly.

lsit.name: L-sit hold on dip bars
lsit.cue: Legs straight and level with the hips; push the bars down so the shoulders stay low. Tuck if the lower back rounds. Tuck-to-L attempts are fine.

alts.name: Tuck-sit
alts.detail: Knees tucked to the chest.

alts.name: One-leg-extended L-sit
alts.detail: Extend one leg at a time.

alts.name: L-sit with 3-second compression lifts
alts.detail: From the L, lift the legs a few cm higher and hold.

alts.name: Floor tuck-sit
alts.detail: Hands flat on the floor beside the hips, press down to lift the hips and tuck the knees. Shoulders pushed down, back rounded slightly.

ringrow.name: Ring rows
ringrow.cue: Body in a straight line throughout. Pull the chest to the rings, not just the hands. Pull past the rings touching the chest — full range.

alts.name: Ring rows with bent knees
alts.detail: Feet closer, knees bent.

alts.name: Feet-elevated ring rows
alts.detail: Feet on a chair. Much harder.

alts.name: Ring rows with 2s pause
alts.detail: Pause 2 seconds with the chest at the rings.

alts.name: Supinated ring rows
alts.detail: Palms facing you — more biceps and lower lats.

alts.name: Table row (inverted row)
alts.detail: Lie under a sturdy table, grip the edge, and pull your chest to the edge with a straight body. Test the table's stability first.

alts.name: Band row
alts.detail: Anchor a band at chest height, sit or stand tall and pull the elbows back to the ribs. Squeeze the shoulder blades together.

alts.name: Dumbbell row
alts.detail: One hand and knee on a chair, back flat. Row the dumbbell to the hip, elbow close to the body, then lower slowly.

archerrow.name: Archer ring rows
archerrow.cue: One arm does most of the work; the other arm stays extended as a guide. Builds the unilateral pulling control needed for dynamic climbing.

alts.name: Ring rows with a staggered grip
alts.detail: One hand higher on the rings, the other lower.

alts.name: One-arm ring row (assisted)
alts.detail: Free hand holds the strap just above the working hand.

alts.name: Archer pull-ups (assisted)
alts.detail: Wide hands on the bar, pull to one side and keep the other arm straight.

alts.name: Band row
alts.detail: Anchor a band at chest height, sit or stand tall and pull the elbows back to the ribs. Squeeze the shoulder blades together.

alts.name: Dumbbell row
alts.detail: One hand and knee on a chair, back flat. Row the dumbbell to the hip, elbow close to the body, then lower slowly.

pullups.name: Pull-ups
pullups.cue: Full range: dead hang at the bottom, chin clears the bar at the top. Shoulders down and back at the start of every rep; no kipping.

alts.name: Band-assisted pull-ups
alts.detail: Loop a band around the bar and one foot; reduce the band as you get stronger.

alts.name: Pull-up negatives
alts.detail: Jump or step to the top and lower as slowly as possible (8–10 seconds).

alts.name: Weighted pull-ups
alts.detail: Backpack with 5–10kg. Only if you can do 3×6 bodyweight pull-ups with clean form.

alts.name: Pull-ups with 2s pause
alts.detail: Pause 2 seconds with the chin over the bar.

alts.name: Typewriter pull-ups (assisted)
alts.detail: At the top, shift your head side to side — the lock-off builds strength fast.

alts.name: Neutral-grip pull-ups
alts.detail: Use a neutral grip on rings or parallel handles.

alts.name: Wide-grip pull-ups
alts.detail: Hands wider than the shoulders. Shorter range, more lat.

alts.name: Band lat pulldown
alts.detail: Anchor a band high on a door. Kneel facing it, arms straight, and pull the elbows down to the ribs without leaning back.

negatives.name: Pull-up negatives
negatives.cue: Jump or step to chin-over-bar. Lower as slowly as possible — target 8–10 seconds. Catch yourself at the bottom, reset. Expect arm fatigue — this is correct.

alts.name: Band-assisted negatives
alts.detail: Add a band to make the descent more controlled.

alts.name: Negatives with a 2-second mid-pause
alts.detail: Stop at the halfway point for 2 seconds.

alts.name: Ring negatives
alts.detail: Do them on rings for a different stability demand.

scap.name: Scapular pull-ups
scap.cue: Start in a true dead hang, arms fully straight. Pull the shoulder blades DOWN only — the arms stay straight and the body rises slightly. This is the foundation of all pull-up work.

alts.name: Active hang
alts.detail: Hold the scapular pull position for 10–15s.

alts.name: Ring scapular pulls
alts.detail: Same, on rings.

deadhang.name: Dead hang holds
deadhang.cue: Completely straight arms, shoulders relaxed (active toward the end). This builds tendon health and grip simultaneously. Stop before the fingers or shoulders ache.

alts.name: Feet-assisted hang
alts.detail: Keep your feet on the floor or a chair to unload the grip.

alts.name: Active hang
alts.detail: Shoulders down and away from the ears; hang 10–15s.

alts.name: Towel hang
alts.detail: Drape a towel over the bar and hold the ends — thicker grip.

alts.name: Ring hang
alts.detail: Hang from rings, turning them out slightly.

lockoff.name: Lock-off holds
lockoff.cue: Step or jump to the top position and hold the lock-off for the prescribed time: chin over the bar. Don't shrug. Lower slowly over 5 seconds. Lock-off strength is what holds your body in on hard moves.

alts.name: 90° lock-off hold
alts.detail: Hold with the elbows at 90° rather than chin over.

alts.name: Lock-off holds at 90° and chin level
alts.detail: Hold 5s at 90° and 5s chin over in one rep.

alts.name: Offset lock-off
alts.detail: Place one hand higher on the bar; alternate sides each set.

alts.name: Ring lock-off holds
alts.detail: Do the same on rings.

tuckfl.name: Tuck front lever
tuckfl.cue: Hang from the bar or rings with arms straight, pull the knees to the chest and lift the hips until the back is horizontal. Hold with the shoulders pulled down. If the hips sag, bend the arms slightly or use a band for assistance. Lat and core strength for steep climbing.

alts.name: Tuck front lever raises
alts.detail: From a hang, lift the knees to the chest and pull the hips up; lower slowly.

alts.name: Band-assisted tuck front lever
alts.detail: Loop a band across the hips and anchor it above.

alts.name: Advanced tuck front lever
alts.detail: Open the hips slightly so the back is flat.

alts.name: Active hang with leg raises
alts.detail: Pull the legs to 90° with straight arms and a stable core.

facepull.name: Band face pulls
facepull.cue: Pull to face height leading with the elbows. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end of each rep.

alts.name: Face pulls with 2s pause
alts.detail: Pause 2 seconds at the end of every rep.

alts.name: Prone Y-T-W raises
alts.detail: Lie face down on the mat and raise the arms into a Y, T and W shape.

alts.name: Band reverse fly
alts.detail: Arms straight, pull the band apart at shoulder height.

ringfacepull.name: Ring face pulls
ringfacepull.cue: Lean back holding the rings, pull the rings to face height leading with the elbows. Squeeze the shoulder blades.

alts.name: Band face pulls
alts.detail: Same movement with a band.

alts.name: Feet-elevated ring face pulls
alts.detail: Feet on a chair. The body is more horizontal.

pullapart.name: Band pull-aparts
pullapart.cue: Arms straight at chest height, pull the band apart, squeeze the shoulder blades.

alts.name: Pull-aparts with 2s pause
alts.detail: Pause at the end of each rep.

alts.name: Overhead pull-aparts
alts.detail: Hold the band overhead and pull apart; opens the upper back.

alts.name: Prone Y-T-W raises
alts.detail: Lie face down on the mat. Lift the arms into a Y, then a T, then a W, thumbs up, pausing 1 second each.

extrot.name: Band external rotation
extrot.cue: Elbow pinned at the side, forearm rotates outward slowly. Protect the rotator cuff.

alts.name: External rotation at 90°
alts.detail: Elbow at shoulder height, forearm rotating up like a hand raise.

alts.name: Prone T raises
alts.detail: Lie face down; raise the arms to a T with thumbs up.

alts.name: External rotation with 3s lowering
alts.detail: Take 3 seconds returning the band.

table_row.name: Table row (inverted row)
table_row.cue: Lie under a sturdy table, grip the edge, and pull your chest to the edge with a straight body. Test the table's stability first.

alts.name: Table row with bent knees
alts.detail: Feet closer, knees bent to reduce the load.

band_row.name: Band row
band_row.cue: Anchor a band at chest height, sit or stand tall and pull the elbows back to the ribs. Squeeze the shoulder blades together.

band_pulldown.name: Band lat pulldown
band_pulldown.cue: Anchor a band high on a door. Kneel facing it, arms straight, and pull the elbows down to the ribs without leaning back.

db_row.name: Dumbbell row
db_row.cue: One hand and knee on a chair, back flat. Row the dumbbell to the hip, elbow close to the body, then lower slowly.

prone_ytw.name: Prone Y-T-W raises
prone_ytw.cue: Lie face down on the mat. Lift the arms into a Y, then a T, then a W, thumbs up, pausing 1 second each.

close_pushup.name: Close-grip push-ups
close_pushup.cue: Hands under the chest, elbows brushing the ribs. Triceps-focused. Use fists if the wrists are sore.

chair_dip.name: Chair dips
chair_dip.cue: Hands on the edge of a sturdy chair, legs bent, lower to about 90° and press back up. Stop if the shoulders pinch.

floor_tuck.name: Floor tuck-sit
floor_tuck.cue: Hands flat on the floor beside the hips, press down to lift the hips and tuck the knees. Shoulders pushed down, back rounded slightly.

db_press.name: Dumbbell floor press
db_press.cue: Lie on the floor, elbows at about 45°, press the dumbbells up and lower until the upper arms touch the floor.

db_ohp.name: Dumbbell overhead press
db_ohp.cue: Stand tall, ribs down, press the dumbbells overhead without arching the lower back. Lower with control.

db_split.name: Dumbbell split squat
db_split.cue: Rear foot on a chair, a dumbbell in each hand, torso upright. Lower straight down and drive up through the front heel.

db_lunge.name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
db_lunge.cue: Dumbbells at your sides. Step back, lower, and drive up through the front heel. Keep the torso tall.

db_rdl.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
db_rdl.cue: Soft knees, dumbbells close to the legs, push the hips back with a flat back to mid-shin, then drive the hips forward. Stop at once if sciatic symptoms appear.

db_hipthrust.name: Dumbbell hip thrust
db_hipthrust.cue: Upper back on a chair or sofa, dumbbell across the hips (padded). Drive the hips to a flat line, squeeze for 1 second, lower slowly.

plank_tap.name: Plank shoulder taps
plank_tap.cue: High plank with feet wide. Tap alternate shoulders without letting the hips rotate. Slow and square.

db_carry.name: Dumbbell suitcase carry
db_carry.cue: One dumbbell in one hand, walk tall without leaning away from the weight. Ribs stacked over hips.

tests.name: Resting heart rate
tests.how: Lie down for 5 minutes on waking, before caffeine. Count beats for 60 seconds (or use a watch). Use the lowest of two mornings.
tests.advice: A lower resting heart rate tracks aerobic fitness and recovery. If it rises 5+ bpm for several days you're under-recovered.

tests.name: Ankle knee-to-wall
tests.how: Toes against a wall, bend the knee to touch the wall with the heel flat. Move the foot back until you can just touch. Measure the toe-to-wall distance for each side.
tests.advice: Ankle range controls how deep you can get a high foot and how well the knee tracks on step-ups and squats.

tests.name: Sit-and-reach
tests.how: Sit with legs straight, feet against a box or wall, reach forward with both hands. Measure how far past the toes you reach (negative if short). Sit on a cushion if the tailbone is sore.
tests.advice: A short result usually means tight hamstrings and calves — relevant to sciatica load, high-foot moves and hip hinges.

tests.name: Overhead wall reach
tests.how: Back, heels and ribs flat against a wall. Raise both arms overhead without letting the lower back arch off the wall. Measure the gap from wrists to wall.
tests.advice: A big gap means limited thoracic and shoulder range, which shows up as arched backs on overhangs and shoulder pinching.

tests.name: Max push-ups
tests.how: Chest to a fist-height target on the floor, full lockout, straight body line. Stop at the first rep that breaks form. Use fists if the wrists are sore.
tests.advice: Pushing endurance protects the shoulders and balances the pulling load.

tests.name: Max bar dips
tests.how: Parallel bars or straight bar, lower to 90° elbows, full lockout, no swinging.
tests.advice: Dip strength builds the triceps and shoulder stability that support heavy pulling.

tests.name: Hollow body hold
tests.how: Lower back flat on the mat, arms overhead, legs low (about 30°). Time until the lower back lifts off the mat.
tests.advice: Hollow tension is the shape you hold on every overhang. Short holds mean the core drops out under load.

tests.name: Side plank
tests.how: Forearm on the mat, feet stacked, hips lifted in a straight line. Time until the hips drop. Test both sides.
tests.advice: Lateral core strength stabilises the pelvis on steep walls, board trim and harness pull. Big left/right gaps matter.

tests.name: L-sit / tuck-sit hold
tests.how: On parallel bars or two chairs, arms locked, legs level (or knees tucked if you can't extend). Time until the legs drop or the shoulders shrug.
tests.advice: Compression strength for high steps and body tension, plus shoulder depression.

tests.name: Bulgarian split squat (bodyweight)
tests.how: Rear foot on a chair, bodyweight only, 2 seconds down, full depth. Count clean reps per leg. Stop if the tailbone or knee hurts.
tests.advice: Single-leg strength drives high-steps, rock-overs and board stance. Check for a weak side.

tests.name: Single-leg calf raises
tests.how: One foot on the edge of a step, full range, 1 second up, 1 second down. Count reps per leg to failure.
tests.advice: Calf and foot strength is stability on small footholds and protects the Achilles.

tests.name: Single-leg glute bridge (feet elevated)
tests.how: Working heel on a low chair, other leg held straight, full hip extension, ribs down. Count reps per leg to failure.
tests.advice: Glutes and hamstrings take load off the lower back. A weak side often shows as a hip shift in squats and hinges.

tests.name: Max strict pull-ups
tests.how: Dead hang start, chin clears the bar, no kipping, controlled lowering to straight arms. Stop at the first rep that breaks form.
tests.advice: Pull-up reps are the clearest predictor of steep-wall power. Below 4, build negatives and lock-offs before adding volume.

tests.name: Lock-off hold (90° elbows)
tests.how: Step up to the bar and hold with elbows at 90°, chin level with the bar. Time until the elbows open or the chin drops.
tests.advice: Lock-off endurance is what holds you in on hard moves. Short holds usually point to weak mid-range pulling.

tests.name: Active dead hang (bar, open hand)
tests.how: Hang from a pull-up bar with an open-hand grip, shoulders active (down and away from the ears). Time until you let go. Stop early if a finger joint hurts.
tests.advice: Grip endurance and finger tendon capacity. Stay in the pain-free range — the capsulitis rules apply.

tests.name: Bouldering grade (V)
tests.how: Highest V-grade you can send within 3 attempts (just the number, e.g. 6 for V6). Same wall each time.
tests.advice: If grades lag the strength tests, the limiter is technique or tactics — use the skill drills.

tests.name: Lead grade (Ewbank)
tests.how: Highest lead grade redpointed within 3 attempts (just the number).
tests.advice: If lead lags bouldering, work on endurance and pump management: 4×4s and rest-position drills.

test_guide: Test on a rested day (a deload week or the day after a rest day) and warm up with Pre-climb Variant A.
Run the tests in the order shown: mobility screens, push, core, legs, then pulling and hangs last, with 2–3 minutes between tests.
Test the same way each time — same bar, same time of day, same warm-up. A different bar thickness changes the hang result.
Stop at the first rep that breaks form, and stop immediately for pain. Levels are approximate bands for a climber at your current grade, not pass/fail marks.
Skip a test if something is sore; the report works with whatever you record.
